pred_ddx.label: Retroperitoneal lymphoma with secondary myositis and skin infiltration

Cutaneous lymphoma: The patient's skin biopsy shows a sparse perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of enlarged atypical mononuclear cells, consistent with cutaneous lymphoma. The patient's systemic symptoms and lack of improvement with antibiotics also support this diagnosis.
Retroperitoneal lymphoma with secondary: The patient's history of incidentally noted bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses, along with the patient's systemic symptoms and muscle enzyme elevations, suggests a retroperitoneal malignancy. The skin biopsy findings and myositis are consistent with secondary involvement of the skin and muscles due to the underlying lymphoma.
